requirement.source: UR I2 Structural Requirements for Polar Class Ships
requirement.text:
I2.9.4 To prevent local flange buckling of welded profiles, the following are to be satisfied:

         (i) The flange width, bf [mm], is not to be less than five times the net thickness of the web,
         twn.
requirement.normalized: For welded profiles, the flange width bf [mm] is not to be less than five times the net web thickness twn [mm] (I2.9.4(i)).

schema_terms.evidenceExcerpt: [I2-019] (ii) In the event that a structural member spans across the boundary of a hull area, the largest hull area factor is to be used in the scantling determination of the member. | [I2-026] The strength of a framing member is dependent upon the fixity that is provided at its supports. Fixity can be assumed where framing members are either continuous through the support or attached to a supporting section with a connection bracket. In other cases, simple support is to be assumed unless the connection can be demonstrated to provide significant rotational restraint. Fixity is to be ensured at the support of any framing which terminates within an ice-strengthened area. | [I2-029] When calculating the section modulus and shear area of a framing member, net thicknesses of the web, flange (if fitted) and attached shell plating are to be used. The shear area of a framing member may include that material contained over the full depth of the member, i.e. web area including portion of flange, if fitted, but excluding attached shell plating. | [I2-031] The local frames in bottom structures (i.e. hull areas BIb, Mb and Sb) and transverse local frames in side structures are to be dimensioned such that the combined effects of shear and bending do not exceed the plastic strength of the member. The plastic strength is defined by the magnitude of midspan load that causes the development of a plastic collapse mechanism. For bottom structure the patch load shall be applied with the dimension (b) parallel with the frame direction. | [I2-034] Longitudinal local frames in side structures are to be dimensioned such that the combined effects of shear and bending do not exceed the plastic strength of the member. The plastic strength is defined by the magnitude of midspan load that causes the development of a plastic collapse mechanism. | [I2-060] The loads carried by a member in way of cut-outs are not to cause instability. Where necessary, the structure is to be stiffened. | [I2-064] For linear structural calculations: web plates and flange elements in compression and shear shall meet the applicable buckling criteria; nominal shear stress in member webs shall be less than sigma_y/sqrt(3); and nominal von Mises stress in member flanges shall be less than 1.15*sigma_y.

schema_terms.evidenceExcerpt: [I2-029] When calculating the section modulus and shear area of a framing member, net thicknesses of the web, flange (if fitted) and attached shell plating are to be used. The shear area of a framing member may include that material contained over the full depth of the member, i.e. web area including portion of flange, if fitted, but excluding attached shell plating. | [I2-030] When the local-frame area exceeds the attached-plate-flange area, z_na = (100*A_fn + h_w*t_wn - 1000*t_pn*s)/(2*t_wn) [mm]. The net effective plastic section modulus is Z_p = t_pn*s*(z_na + t_pn/2)*sin(phi_w) + (((h_w - z_na)^2 + z_na^2)*t_wn*sin(phi_w))/2000 + A_fn*((h_fc - z_na)*sin(phi_w) - b_w*cos(phi_w))/10 [cm^3]. For oblique framing (70 deg > Omega > 20 deg), use linear interpolation. | [I2-040] To prevent local web buckling, h_w/t_wn <= 282/sqrt(sigma_y) for flat-bar sections and h_w/t_wn <= 805/sqrt(sigma_y) for bulb, tee and angle sections. | [I2-041] In addition, the net web thickness shall satisfy t_wn >= 0.35*t_pn*sqrt(sigma_y/235), where sigma_y is the minimum upper yield stress of the shell plate and t_pn is the net shell-plate thickness in way of the framing member. | [I2-042] (i) The flange width, bf [mm], is not to be less than five times the net thickness of the web, twn.

contract.comparisonModel: For source-applicable welded profiles, flangeWidth >= 5*netWebThickness. The mapping of welded applicability to the generic structuralMember inventory is unresolved.
contract.formulaExpression: flangeWidth >= 5*netWebThickness, restricted to applicable welded profiles; do not assume all structuralMember nodes qualify.

sourceBackedObligations.description: For applicable welded profiles, flange width is not less than five times net web thickness; equality is permitted. Do not reverse the inequality or require a member instance from this universal alone.

contract.verificationScope: Subclause (i) minimum flange/web ratio only. Full source limits the clause to welded profiles; generic structuralMember inventory does not establish this eligibility.
contract.sourceApplicabilityPrecondition: Polar Class population plus welded-profile applicability; the latter is not represented by an explicit selector or scoped member class.
